development_status: The policy and budget B=32 are post-hoc development choices informed by 84 previously observed cases: original v0 n12/n14 cases, C588 quartic n16, and the v2 multi-family n16 transfer set. On those development cases the policy matched per-case min(two_arm,always_three) live nodes while reducing always-three candidate compilations by 13.9% to 21.3% across cohorts. Those cases are not confirmatory evidence for this policy.
purpose: Confirm or falsify a progressive value-of-computation controller that buys only a 32-neighbor seeded probe first, completes the full seeded first stage only when that probe already beats the best conventional one-stage arm, and otherwise avoids the remaining seeded neighborhood. This directly targets final policy utility rather than the earlier one-stage seeded-winner classifier.
canonicalization: Wrap every generated graph as nx.Graph(generator_output) before deriving natural/RCM/seeded orders.

seeded_start.choice: same max-min normalized Kendall rule as v0

local_search.neighborhood: all distinct one-variable remove-and-reinsert orders in the existing deterministic enumeration
local_search.selection: min live then allocated then lexicographic

probe_complete_policy.probe_unit: first 32 eligible seeded-neighborhood candidates after compiling the seeded start once
probe_complete_policy.conventional_work: run one full local-search stage on natural and RCM first
probe_complete_policy.trigger: if best seeded start/probe live nodes is strictly lower than the best conventional one-stage live nodes, evaluate the remaining eligible seeded neighbors to complete the exact seeded first stage; otherwise skip them
probe_complete_policy.reuse: probe candidate evaluations are reused and never recomputed when the seeded stage is completed
probe_complete_policy.commit: after the conditional seeded completion, choose the best staged arm using the existing live/candidate-cost/fixed-priority rule and continue only that arm to at most 2 accepted moves total

offline_baselines.per_case_quality_oracle: min(final two_arm live nodes, final always_three live nodes); this oracle is for evaluation only and is not available to the deployed probe policy

co_primary_criteria.quality: summed probe-complete final live nodes must equal the summed per-case quality oracle, with zero positive per-case regret
co_primary_criteria.charged_compute: probe-complete candidate compilations must be at least 10% lower than always_three across all 24 cases

predeclared_tests: Report overall and family-stratified trigger rate, candidate compilations, final live-node sum, regret versus per-case min(two,three), and every positive-regret case.
Report every case where always_three strictly beats two_arm and whether the probe triggered; if no such cases occur, seeded-benefit retention is inconclusive rather than established.
Report every case where always_three is worse than two_arm and whether the probe avoided or reproduced the harm.
Compare against two_arm and always_three on identical cases; width+1 and frozen learned gates may be reported only as secondary historical diagnostics, not tuned on this split.

All conventional and probe-complete completed endpoints must match invariant Hamming rank; each distinct final endpoint must additionally match an exhaustive direct truth-bitset oracle in its own relabeled coordinates.
Do not change B=32, enumeration, trigger, seeds, generators or criteria after outcomes. Any revision requires a new untouched split.
decision_rule: The probe-complete policy is confirmed on this holdout only if both co-primary criteria pass. Compute savings with any positive quality regret is a failure; zero regret without at least 10% savings is also a failure.
scope: Synthetic positive-monotone graph 2-CNF ROBDD ordering on these 24 fixed n=18 cases only. This is a test-time search controller experiment, not a general proof-search claim.
